{{Short description|Italian CDI researcher and physicist}}
{{Orphan|date=December 2019}}

'''Valeria Pettorino''' is an Italian physicist working in [[cosmology]], [[astrophysics]] and [[data analysis]]. She is a CDI Researcher at CosmoStat, CEA [[Saclay]],<ref name="interview2">(8 October 2017). [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BPy7j3aEWi4 The launch of Sputnik1 - Astrophysicist Valeria Pettorino], ''[[Radio France Internationale|RFI English]]'' (interview with Petterino confirms her current placements)</ref> and she is part of Planck and Euclid [[European Space Agency|ESA]]/[[NASA]] international space missions.

Her work is related to the use of data from ground and space missions to test theoretical models that describe the evolution and content of the Universe. Her work aims to describe the  nature of [[dark matter]] and [[dark energy]].

== Career ==
Pettorino studied physics as an undergraduate and obtained her PhD from the [[University of Naples Federico II|University of Naples]] in 2005, with a dissertation on "Dark energy in generalized theories of gravity".<ref name="quanta">{{Cite news|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/cosmologist-valeria-pettorino-wanders-in-dantes-dark-wood-20181113/?mc_cid=fb7cfadb0d&mc_eid=563d664ed9|title=Cosmologist Valeria Pettorino Wanders in Dante's Dark Wood {{!}} Quanta Magazine|work=Quanta Magazine|access-date=2018-11-17}}</ref> In 2007 she joined the [[Euclid (spacecraft)|Euclid space mission]] and became an Alexander von Humboldt Fellow at the [[Heidelberg University|University of Heidelberg]]. In 2009 she joined the [[Planck space mission]] and became Associate Research Fellow at [[Columbia University]]. She completed her PostDoc at [[International School for Advanced Studies|SISSA]] in Trieste.

She works as astrophysicist and research engineer at CEA Paris-Saclay. Pettorino helped complete the final analysis of data from the [[European Space Agency]]’s Planck space telescope, which mapped the early universe with unprecedented precision.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cosmos.esa.int/web/planck/publications|title=Publications - Cosmos|website=www.cosmos.esa.int|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-11-17}}</ref>

Pettorino is also on the leadership team for the Worldwide Mentorship Program for Women in Physics.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://valeriapettorino.wixsite.com/website/fullscreen-page/comp-jkv78znr2/fee048b2-d589-46b6-8385-bdb62824e22f/4/?i=4&p=qtq42&s=style-jkv78znt|title=My homepage {{!}} Fullscreen Page|work=Home {{!}} Valeria Pettorino|access-date=2018-11-17|language=it}}</ref> She also helped organize the annual EuroPython conference for users of the [[Python (programming language)|Python]] programming language.

==Personal==
Pettorino's uncle was physicist Roberto Pettorino (1946-2013), who worked in string theory.<ref name="quanta"/><ref name="roberto1">[https://www.sif.it/riviste/sif/sag/ricordo/pettorino In ricordo di Roberto Pettorino (1946-2013)], [[Italian Physical Society]] (in Italian), Retrieved 13 December 2013</ref> As a side project, Pettorino took part into a creative writing group project, where she translated the opening lines of Dante’s ''Divine Comedy'' into a geometry problem.<ref>{{Cite web|title=quantamagazine|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/cosmologist-valeria-pettorino-wanders-in-dantes-dark-wood-20181113/|last=|first=|date=13 November 2018|website=quantamagazine|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

*with  Austin Peel, Florian Lalande, Jean-Luc Starck, Julian Merten, Carlo Giocoli, Massimo Meneghetti, Marco Baldi: ''Distinguishing standard and modified gravity cosmologies with machine learning (2018)''
* with Julian Merten, Carlo Giocoli, Marco Baldi, Massimo Meneghetti, Austin Peel, Florian Lalande, Jean-Luc Starck: ''On the dissection of degenerate cosmologies with machine learning (2018)''
* with Austin Peel, Valeria Pettorino, Carlo Giocoli, Jean-Luc Starck, Marco Baldi: ''Breaking degeneracies in modified gravity with higher (than 2nd) order weak-lensing statistics'' (2018)
* with Santiago Casas, Martin Kunz, Matteo Martinelli: ''Linear and non-linear Modified Gravity forecasts with future surveys'' (2017)
